notes: Both tools are registered unconditionally at server construction (`Zt`), except `download_figma_images` which is gated by `skipImageDownloads`.

The bundle's `dist/chunk-CPSYXR2U.js` (`he` path validation) and `dist/common-HYY6FKF5.js` (`downloadFigmaImage`) were not provided; the path-containment and download behaviour is judged from call sites and the error cases (`outside_image_dir`) in dist/chunk-E7X4SVMG.js:1.

HTTP transport listens on FRAMELINK_HOST/FRAMELINK_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:3333) and accepts per-request Figma tokens via headers; this changes whose data the SECRET label covers but not the labels themselves.

download_figma_images.rationale: `Bt` validates `localPath` with `he(u,d)` against the configured `imageDir` (rejecting `outside_image_dir`/`drive_letter_on_posix`), then `Ze` -> `X.downloadImages` -> `W` -> `downloadFigmaImage` fetches only URLs returned by the Figma API (`getImageFillUrls`/`getNodeRenderUrls`), never an agent-supplied URL, so no SINK. It writes/overwrites image files (extension constrained to png|svg|gif by `fileName` regex) inside the image directory and crops them via `je`/`Ft`, which is confined file I/O, not host code execution. The tool result contains only file basenames and pixel dimensions (`finalDimensions`, `cssVariables`), not Figma file content, so it does not return secret or attacker-controlled text into context.

get_figma_data.rationale: `get_figma_data` calls `X.getRawFile`/`getRawNode` -> `requestWithSize` -> `Ke` (fetch) against `https://api.figma.com/v1` with the user's credentials injected by `getAuthHeaders()` (`X-Figma-Token: this.apiKey` or `Authorization: Bearer ${this.oauthToken}`), and returns the simplified/serialized file content (including node `name` and `text` values, see `Oe`/`Ce`) into the agent context — that is private data from the user's Figma account, so SECRET. The `fileKey` is an arbitrary agent-supplied alphanumeric key (`Lt.fileKey`), so the tool can also read any link-shared/community Figma file an attacker published; the returned layer names and text strings are then attacker-controllable, so UNTRUSTED. Error paths also echo the Figma API response body back to the caller (`ce`, `Ot`). Not a SINK: the request target is the fixed vendor host `https://api.figma.com/v1` with only a path/id built from input.

value_conditions.default: false — the image download tool is registered by default
value_conditions.effect: Does not register the `download_figma_images` tool at all (`o.skipImageDownloads||e.registerTool(k.name,...)`).
Sets the root directory that `download_figma_images` may write into; `he(localPath, imageDir)` rejects paths resolving outside it.

value_conditions.default: empty; stdio mode refuses to start, HTTP mode falls back to per-request headers
value_conditions.effect: Supplies the credential used for Figma API calls; without it (stdio mode) startup fails via `Ne`, and in HTTP mode per-request `X-Figma-Token`/`Authorization: Bearer` headers are used instead (`so`,`ao`,`lo`), so the SECRET reach follows whichever account's token is presented.

value_conditions.default: no explicit proxy; environment proxy variables are honoured if present
value_conditions.effect: Routes all Figma API and image fetches through the given proxy via `setGlobalDispatcher(new ProxyAgent(...))`/`EnvHttpProxyAgent`; `--proxy=none` disables env proxies.

Disables PostHog telemetry (`V`/`ie`) which otherwise posts tool-call metrics and redacted error messages to the fixed endpoint https://us.i.posthog.com; this is server-side, not a tool-reachable sink.
